history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration provide measurable benchmarks to match the objectives and offer clear guidance to entities in the use of the assessment results of key performance indicator 6.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation implemented and requests its closure. In the second release of the expansion of the delegation of authority key performance indicators (February 2022), key performance indicator 60 was revised, as of the fourth quarter 2021, so as to assist entities in assessing their performance in terms of timely reporting of exceptions (i.e. within four calendar days of the date of the decision to the date of entry in the log). Given the constraints in refining the human resources exceptions log to capture the working days only of each duty station and exclude weekends and official holidays, which vary from one duty station to another, the Business Transformation and Accountability Division extended the reporting compliance from one business day to four calendar days so that, if an office complies with submission within one business day, it will score 100 per cent in the key performance indicator. For example, if an office based in New York grants an exception on a Friday, it should be reported by close of business on Monday at the latest – three calendar days later – unless the Monday is a holiday, in which case it should be reported on the Tuesday, or four calendar days later. Thanks to the changes to this key performance indicator and the introduction of a benchmark, the entities (first line of defence) and the Business Transformation and Accountability Division (second line of defence) can assess their compliance with the four calendar days requirement and compare their performance against that of other similar entities. The human resources exception analysis report for 2021 provides further analysis on the compliance of entities and the overall trends. In addition, the Business Transformation and Accountability Division conducts quarterly reviews of high-volume exceptions by identifying exceptions from data extracted from the enterprise system and comparing with exceptions reported in the log. Non-reported exceptions are brought to the attention of entities.
history.board_assessment: Given that the relevant key performance indicator was revised in the fourth quarter of 2021 so as to assist entities in assessing their performance in terms of timely reporting of exceptions, the Board considers this recommendation implemented.
